title: SmokePath: choose the structure (re-roll 1)
question: Fresh hand; nothing from round one returns. Your DESIGN.md stays the material (dark glass, Mona Sans, one green action, CPCB colours). The roll assigned The Smoke Ticket.

options.label: The Smoke Ticket
options.lineage: the IRCTC e-ticket and PNR status every Indian checks: from, to, arrival, coach, status
options.thesis: Tomorrow's smoke is a journey with a departure, a route and an arrival time at your school, and your timetable is the ticket's status list.
materials: glass ticket with a perforated stub, hairline segments, tabular times
the smoke's back-trajectory drawn as a route with stops on the live map
mono status codes: KEPT · MOVED · INDOORS
options.viewport: Desktop: live map with the smoke route lit from the Punjab fire clusters to Delhi; on the right a glass ticket: FROM Sangrur fires → TO your school, ARRIVES Tue 08:00, then one status line per period, and a stub with the parent message and the one green 'Get alerts'. Phone: route map on top, ticket as a bottom sheet.
options.risk: If the ticket costume outgrows the content it reads as a gimmick; status words must stay plain.

raised.raise: When a school is picked, the map dims everything except its smoke route and its ring.
Ticket segments are divided by 1px hairlines with tabular figures; no boxes inside boxes.
The hourly strip sits on a visible hour grid that the whole ticket snaps to.
A changed period moves to its new slot and stays lit until it has been seen.
Switching Today/Tomorrow flips changed times in place instead of re-rendering the page.

options.label: Counting-Day Map
options.lineage: election-results night on Indian TV: districts colour in as results arrive, a seat tally climbs
options.thesis: Smoke night as results night: schools colour in hour by hour and the tally of affected schools climbs.
materials: full map with a tally bar across the top
search 'find your school' like finding your constituency
options.viewport: Full-bleed map; across the top a tally bar (Severe · Very Poor · Poor schools) that ticks as the timeline plays; a search box finds your school and opens its plan on the side.
options.risk: Familiar TV-results grammar, and election connotations may distract.

options.label: Smoke Metro Map
options.thesis: Smoke routes as metro lines: fire clusters are terminus stations, Delhi's districts are interchanges, your school is a stop.
options.viewport: A diagram of the smoke corridors from Punjab into Delhi over the map; tap your school's 'station' to see its plan.
options.case: Delhi principals know the metro map by heart; the diagram simplifies the real winds, which costs clarity.
options.risk: A schematic can look more certain than a forecast is.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles; the focused one grows, the rest dim.
options.case: Fuses poorly: schools are not titles to browse.

options.label: Design-Annual Plate
options.thesis: Registration marks and hairlines on near-white stock.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a light print world fights your dark DESIGN.md.
options.kept: Hairline-divided segments, tabular figures, no boxes in boxes.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The construction grid as visible armature.
options.case: Fuses poorly: monumental type helps no principal decide.
options.kept: A visible hour grid everything snaps to.

options.label: Boarding Pass + Gate Board
options.thesis: A pass with segments; changed gates move in place and stay lit.
options.viewport: Pass on the left, ranked board on the right.
options.case: Close to the roll but less familiar to Indian schools than a train ticket.
options.kept: A changed row moves and stays lit until seen.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.case: Fuses poorly: a board of rows hides the map story.

canonCard.label: Air-quality dashboard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships: map, sidebar list, big AQI number cards.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar with search and school list, map right, AQI number cards on top.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every AQI app, which you said would feel wrong.
